newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Welteke welcomes greater BoE independence.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Welteke welcomes greater BoE independence.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke on Tuesday welcomed the move by Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer to make the Bank of England more independent.
"It should be welcomed that the Bank of England is becoming more independent," Welteke said in response to reporters' questions.
He said Britain had in the past not met the Maastricht Treaty's fifth convergence criterion -- central bank independence.

But he added that in theory Britain could not be among the first wave of countries to form European economic and monetary union at the scheduled January 1, 1999 start date because it had not met the exchange rate criterion.
Britain's new Chancellor of the Exchequer, Gordon Brown, on Tuesday announced substantial moves towards independence for the Bank of England but stopped short of full autonomy.
The British central bank now has "operational responsibility" for setting interest rates to meet an inflation target laid down by the Treasury.
But the move does not comply with the Maastricht criteria on central bank independence because the Treasury will still determine the inflation aim.
